product: Thai rolled ice cream / stir-fried ice cream (ไอติมผัด · ไอศกรีมผัด, i-tim phat) — liquid dairy base poured onto a steel plate held at roughly −25 to −30 °C, chopped and spread with two scrapers into a ~2–3 mm sheet, then scraped up into tight spirals and stood upright in a cup. Arabic working name for the deck: الآيس كريم المَلْفُوف / آيس كريم الصَّاج البارد.
origin:
ORIGIN — the honest version, which is messier than the marketing version.

CONSENSUS STORY (what every English-language source says): The dessert emerged as Thai street food around 2009 under the name ไอติมผัด / ไอศกรีมผัด ("stir-fried ice cream"), spread into neighbouring Southeast Asian countries, and was an established regional ice-cream style by 2012. It reached the United States in 2015. Sources: English Wikipedia "Stir-fried ice cream"; Tasting Table (tastingtable.com/1598781); The Takeout (thetakeout.com/1716542); Chowhound (chowhound.com/1674827). CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the 2009 date and Thai street-food framing — it is unanimous across food media.

NAMED INVENTOR: The trend is credited to Kajitsa Premwimol, who launched it in Thailand in 2009 under the brand "I-TIM-PAD". In 2015 Premwimol and two college friends — Teeradej Naruenartwanich and Apisit Sutthisophaarpom — brought the concept to New York City as I-CE-NY. The brand claims 250+ locations across Asia and 20+ in the US. Sources: The Takeout, "How Rolled Ice Cream Made Its Way From Thailand To Worldwide Fame"; icenybaldwinpark.com/about; Grokipedia "Stir-fried ice cream". CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. This attribution only appears in 2024–2025 SEO-era food media and AI-written encyclopedia entries. I could not corroborate the name "Kajitsa Premwimol" in any Thai-language source. English Wikipedia itself states it is NOT clear who invented it, when, or where. DO NOT put this name on a slide as settled fact — say "يُنسَب الفضل إلى" (credited to), not "اخترعته".

THE COUNTER-CLAIM THE DECK SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: Chinese Wikipedia's entry for 炒冰 (chǎo bīng, "stir-fried ice") states the technique actually originated in TAIWAN, was carried to Thailand, was developed and popularised there, and only then got renamed 泰式炒冰 — "Thai-style stir-fried ice". Separately, 炒酸奶 (stir-fried yogurt) is credited in Chinese sources to a father-and-son surnamed Tian in Anju, Jining, Shandong, with ice-machine experiments dating to the 1990s that "the public did not accept" at the time. Sources: zh.wikipedia.org/zh-my/炒冰; baike.baidu.com/item/炒酸奶. CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM on the existence of the counter-claim, LOW on its resolution. Practical read for SHABIM: "Thai" is a marketing origin, not a settled historical one — which means nobody owns it, and an Iraqi brand has as much right to it as anyone.

PRICE AT ORIGIN: ~40–60 Thai baht per serving in Bangkok night markets (Chatuchak Weekend Market cited). CONFIDENCE: LOW — single AI-generated source (Grokipedia); treat as illustrative only.

THE PHYSICS: Reuters (via The Star, 1 June 2021) describes the plate as "cooled to minus-30 degrees Celsius". Equipment specs converge: machines are built to reach −25 to −30 °C, but operators typically run the plate surface at −18 to −21 °C in service; commercial pans reach working temperature in about 3 minutes; 304 food-grade stainless plate; 1,500–1,800 W per pan. Sources: thestar.com.my (Reuters, 2021); rollicecream.com "Understanding the Freezing Process"; vevor.com 1800 W 50 cm single-round-pan listing; aussieblends.com/pages/rolled-ice-cream-process. CONFIDENCE: HIGH.
virality:
THE VIRAL CURVE — with names, dates and numbers, including the part that goes down.

═══ PHASE 1 · THE SEED VIDEO (March 2015) ═══
Gil Grobe, a German marketing employee from Hamburg, was in Thailand in MARCH 2015 after attending a friend's wedding in Singapore. He saw a crowd around a street stall and filmed the vendor on his phone. He uploaded the roughly three-minute clip to FACEBOOK first, where it took ~300,000 views and 1,000+ shares before he mirrored it to YouTube. That single holiday clip now sits above 13.6 MILLION views. Sources: web-netz.de interview with Gil Grobe; OMR Daily "Ice Cream Rolls: Hamburger betreibt weltgrößten Youtube-Eis-Channel"; Business Insider Deutschland/Gründerszene; Wikitubia. CONFIDENCE: HIGH on 300k/1,000 shares and 13.6M (multiple independent German-language business outlets).

He then taught himself the technique and turned it into a channel. "Ice Cream Rolls" (YouTube UCAon55hNT6ESbdQ5y1hRWTA, operated as Roll it Media GmbH, Hamburg):
• 10.8 MILLION subscribers as of 1 June 2021 — one of only FOUR Germans with YouTube's Diamond Play Button at the time (Reuters via thestar.com.my, 1 June 2021).
• 12 MILLION+ subscribers now, ~1.73 BILLION lifetime views across 2,490+ videos (vidIQ / CreatorDB / Wikitubia). ~6.25 million views in a recent trailing 30 days (vidIQ).
• Most-viewed single video: "Ice Cream Rolls | Cadbury – Dairy Milk Chocolate Ice Cream / fried Thailand rolled ice cream roll" — 75 MILLION+ views.
• Format: 10 minutes, no music, no talking, pure ASMR scraping sound. Audience concentrated in the US, UK, India and South Korea, not Germany.
• He quit his marketing job and now sells his own proprietary base POWDER for "the perfect Ice Cream Roll consistency" in his own webshop. That detail matters more than the view count — see hard_to_copy.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH on 10.8M/2021 and the Diamond Button (Reuters). MEDIUM on 12M / 1.73B / 75M (aggregator sites, self-consistent across three of them).

═══ PHASE 2 · THE US STOREFRONT MOMENT (August 2015) ═══
10BELOW ICE CREAM, 10 Mott Street, NYC Chinatown. Opened EARLY AUGUST 2015 by Richard Tam, then 23, with two fraternity brothers — all first-time restaurateurs. Tam's stated trigger: he saw a Facebook video of a Thai street vendor doing it. Result: HOUR-LONG lines all day from opening, reported up to THREE-HOUR lines, with effectively zero marketing spend.
• BuzzFeed, Lindsay Hunt, "An NYC Shop Is Making Insane Rolled Ice Cream And It's Mesmerizing" — published 21 AUGUST 2015 (buzzfeed.com/lindsayhunt/10below-rolled-ice-cream). This is the single most-cited piece of coverage in the whole cycle; every later account traces the US explosion back through it.
• Eater NY named 10Below "#1 New Ice Cream Shop in NYC"; TimeOut put it on "Most Instagrammable Foods".
• Food Network ran it twice on Facebook video: "Be mesmerized by Thai-inspired ice cream rolls — 10Below Ice Cream" (facebook.com/FoodNetwork post 10153741670096727, ~2016) and "S'more ice cream rolls at 10Below Ice Cream" (post 10156448843636727, ~2018).
• Sources: BuzzFeed (21 Aug 2015); HuffPost "How Social Media Has Made NYC's Ice-Cream Scene More Innovative Than Ever"; NYU Local; Downtown Magazine; AOL (24 Aug 2015).
HONEST GAP: I could NOT retrieve view counts for the BuzzFeed or Food Network Facebook videos — Facebook video pages are not readable from here and no secondary source reports the figures. Do not invent a number for these. Mark UNSOURCED on the slide or omit.

═══ PHASE 3 · THE US LAND RUSH (2016–2017) ═══
The clearest measurable curve is Philadelphia, from the Philadelphia Inquirer, "Philly's rolled-ice cream craze headed for a melt down?", 29 JUNE 2017:
• APRIL 2016: ZERO places in Philadelphia to buy a $7 cup of custom rolled ice cream.
• JUNE 2017: MORE THAN A DOZEN in the region.
That is 0 → 12+ in ~14 months in one metro. Note the headline: the trade press was already asking about the meltdown at the peak.
New Jersey followed the same shape in 2016 — Absolute Zero (Montclair), Freezing Point (Lyndhurst), ZRolls (Summit) (NJ Monthly).
Google Trends: rolled ice cream was named one of the biggest trends of 2016 with a surge in MAY 2016, and was still among the top-searched ice cream types in JULY 2018 (Google blog, National Ice Cream Day search trends). One AI-written source (accio.com) claims interest kept climbing to a peak in early 2022 — LOW confidence, contradicted by every storefront datapoint below; do not use it.

═══ PHASE 4 · THE ASIA PEAK, WHICH WAS BIGGER THAN THE US ONE (2017) ═══
JAPAN was arguably the loudest single market. ROLL ICE CREAM FACTORY, operated by Trend Factory Inc., opened Japan's first dedicated rolled-ice-cream shop in HARAJUKU/OMOTESANDO on 24 JUNE 2017.
• Queues of up to FIVE HOURS reported at the flagship (one Japanese blog reports seven).
• It landed exactly on インスタ映え ("Instagrammable"), which was Japan's buzzword of the year for 2017.
• Grew to 8 stores nationwide — Osaka Dotonbori, Nagoya, Okinawa Kokusai-dori, Yokohama, Kyoto, Ikebukuro, Fukuoka, plus a Tokushima pop-up — and opened its first overseas store in Taiwan.
Sources: pretty-online.jp; prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000051.000034651; ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ロールアイス; churatoku.net; mynavi.jp "SNSで話題のバズるグルメ(8) #ロールアイス". CONFIDENCE: HIGH.
KOREA: entered as 철판 아이스크림 ("iron-plate ice cream") on the same 2015–2017 wave (Korean wiki entry; Daum shopping magazine feature, 2016). CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM.

═══ PHASE 5 · THE DECLINE — do not soften this ═══
The curve did not plateau. It rolled over.
• SWEET CHARLIE'S (founded 2015, Philadelphia, the biggest US rolled-ice-cream franchise): 3 units in 2017 → 17+ units by 2022 → 13 UNITS TODAY. Franchise Grade currently records a −5% growth rate. Franchise fee $30K; total investment $100K–$400K. Sources: peersense.com/franchise/sweet-charlie-s-franchising-llc; franchisegrade.com/franchises/sweet-charlie-s; ifpg.org. CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH.
• 10BELOW, the shop that started the US wave, now shows multiple PERMANENTLY CLOSED locations on Yelp: 42½ St Marks Place NYC, 132 Allen Street NYC, and 232 E 2nd Street in Little Tokyo, Los Angeles. CONFIDENCE: HIGH (Yelp closure flags).
• I-CE-NY, the founder's own US flagship at 101 MacDougal Street NYC, is listed TEMP. CLOSED on Yelp. CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM.
• JAPAN: ROLL ICE CREAM FACTORY has been contracting — MARK IS Fukuoka Momochi CLOSED 28 AUGUST 2025 after only ~2 years (opened Sept 2023); Ishigaki Coconut Terrace suspended October 2024; the Nagoya LACHIC store is flagged 閉店 (closed). Chain aggregators now list ~7 stores. Sources: fukuokachuo.goguynet.jp (2 Sept 2025); jouhou.nagoya; tapioca-maps.com. CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH.
• Trade framing: rolled ice cream is now named alongside pay-by-weight frozen yogurt as one of the "dessert phenomena" America moved past, which "plummeted" the business models of chains that were built on novelty (eatthis.com, "7 Ice Cream Chains That Crashed and Burned"). CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM (opinion journalism, but it is the industry consensus).
• The only growth number left is EQUIPMENT, not dessert: the Rolled Ice Cream Maker market is put at $150M (2024) → $300M (2033), 8.5% CAGR (verifiedmarketreports.com). CONFIDENCE: LOW — syndicated market report, unverifiable methodology. Note what it actually means: the machines are selling, which is a commoditisation signal, not a brand-value signal.

═══ HASHTAGS — read this before putting any hashtag number on a slide ═══
Hashtag totals for this product are NOT reliably obtainable in 2026, and the deck should say so rather than fake precision:
• TikTok removed public hashtag VIEW counters in 2024 (it now surfaces post counts inconsistently), and Instagram deprecated public hashtag post counts and hashtag browsing in December 2024. Any "#rolledicecream = X billion views" figure circulating today is a fossil from before that change.
• The only figure I could surface: accio.com states #RolledIceCream has 47.9 MILLION POSTS on TikTok. CONFIDENCE: LOW — accio.com is AI-generated commerce content, the figure is implausibly large for the niche, and I could not corroborate it anywhere. If used, label it "hashtag aggregate, unverified, single AI-generated source."
• For scale context only, as a HASHTAG AGGREGATE not a single video: #icecream on TikTok is reported at 3.1M posts / 61.8 BILLION cumulative views, with #IceCreamRolls and #ThaiIceCream listed among its top related tags (tiktokhashtags.com/hashtag/icecream). CONFIDENCE: LOW-MEDIUM.
• MEANING-DRIFT FINDING, and this one is genuinely useful: searching the Arabic phrase "ايس كريم رول" on TikTok today returns overwhelmingly the FRUIT ROLL-UP ice cream hack (#rollups, #rollupschallenge, #ترند_rollups) — an unrelated American snack trend — not Thai pan-rolled ice cream. In Arabic social search, the phrase has been colonised by something else. SHABIM cannot rely on that keyword for discovery.

═══ IS IT STILL VIRAL IN MENA? — mixed, and worth being precise about ═══
TURKEY — YES, and it is institutionalised, not trend-dependent. Turkish has settled vocabulary for it: rulo dondurma, tava dondurma, Tayland usulü dondurma. Arsoni has been MANUFACTURING Thai/rolled ice cream machines domestically SINCE 2014 and franchises under its own ICE FRUTTI brand; Doğuş Makina runs a dedicated site (tavadondurmam.com) selling machines, pans and base powder. "Thai Roll Ice / Tava Dondurma" franchises in Istanbul at an entry investment of just 15,000–25,000 TL. Türkiye Gazetesi ran a Facebook explainer video on it. Sources: arsoni.com.tr; franchiseturkey.com/thai-roll-ice-tava-dondurma-franchise-bayiligi; iskuruyorum.com; facebook.com/turkiyegazetesi. READ: Turkey has domesticated it into cheap commodity infrastructure — which is exactly why it is no longer premium there.
GULF — PRESENT, NOT DOMINANT. JAM Rolled Icecream in Bur Dubai is explicitly positioned as Thai-origin, with rolls served in tacos (AED 30), cups (AED 25), waffles (AED 35) and milkshakes (AED 20) — evidence the Gulf market monetises it through FORMAT VARIETY, not through the roll alone. Rolled-ice-cream stalls operate seasonally at Global Village Dubai ("Tawa Ice Cream"). Gulfood 2026 lists an "Arabian Ice Cream Roll" product. Sources: tripadvisor JAM Rolled Icecream; curlytales.com; gulfood.com/gulfood-2026-products/arabian-ice-cream-roll; tauyanm.com. CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. I found NO evidence of a rolled-ice-cream chain of scale in Riyadh or Jeddah.
EGYPT — PRESENT, FRAGMENTED, AND ALREADY SHRINKING. "Ice Roll" operates in Zahraa El-Maadi, Cairo — inside a petrol station (Yellow Pages Egypt, profile 616758). "Ice Cream Roll & More" had a Downtown Cairo branch at Midan Orabi, Azbakeya, listed CLOSED on elmenus, plus a Hadayek El-Ahram branch. Machines are sold heavily on Dubizzle Egypt and Amazon.eg. So: cheap machines everywhere, no brand of scale, and the flagship downtown location is dead.
IRAQ — THE HONEST FINDING: IT NEVER PROPERLY LANDED.
Evidence it exists at all, and it is thin: a Facebook page "IceRoll Baghdad – ايس رول بغداد", an Instagram account "ICEROLL IRAQ" (@ice_rolliraq), and rolled-ice-cream machines listed for sale on OpenSooq Baghdad. That is the entire footprint I could find.
Evidence it did NOT land:
(a) Rolled ice cream appears NOWHERE in Iraqi press coverage of Baghdad's dessert scene. Iraqi News's "The Best Cafés in Baghdad 2024" is entirely coffee-and-café — Al-Reef in Karrada, ZOKA — with no rolled ice cream.
(b) Baghdad's ice-cream identity is already occupied by four other categories: traditional Iraqi/dondurma (Al-Faqma, Al-Saiha, Baghdad Ice Cream), Italian gelato (Biscotti Iraq), American chains (Cold Stone Creamery Iraq), and industrial (Grand Dairy, Ice King).
(c) CRITICAL BRANDING HAZARD: in Iraqi menus, "ايس رول" ALREADY MEANS SOMETHING ELSE — a rolled-wafer ice cream item. Baghdad Ice Cream's own online menu lists "الايس رول" as a category containing "ايس رول مكسرات" (nut ice roll). The name is taken, by a completely different product.
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH on "never properly landed" (absence of evidence across press, listings and directories is strong here); HIGH on the name-collision, which is directly verifiable from the Baghdad Ice Cream menu URL.
STRATEGIC READ FOR THE DECK: Iraq is the one market in the region where this product has NOT been burned out by a 2017 boom-and-bust, because it never had one. SHABIM would not be riding a dead Western trend — it would be introducing a nine-year-old proven Asian format into a market whose only exposure is a handful of unbranded stalls and a name-collision. But it must NOT be sold as "the viral thing from TikTok." That story is over everywhere else, and Baghdad customers who travel to Dubai, Istanbul and Cairo have seen the commodity version. Sell the craft, the base, and the cold — not the trend.

hard_to_copy:
WHAT IS STRUCTURALLY HARD TO COPY — and, honestly, what is not.

NOT DEFENSIBLE (say this out loud in the deck, or an investor will say it for you):
• The MACHINE is a commodity. VEVOR sells a 1,800 W, 50 cm single-round-pan commercial unit off the shelf; Amazon.sa and Amazon.eg both stock Thai rolled-ice-cream machines for consumers; Arsoni and Doğuş Makina mass-produce them in Turkey; machines are listed on OpenSooq Baghdad and Dubizzle Egypt. A Turkish rolled-ice-cream franchise entry costs 15,000–25,000 TL total.
• The TECHNIQUE is free. There are 2,490+ instructional/ASMR videos on one YouTube channel alone, plus a decade of tutorials. Nothing is secret.
Anyone claiming the roll itself is a moat is wrong.

ACTUALLY DEFENSIBLE — four real barriers:

1. THE BASE FORMULATION IS THE REAL IP. The sheet only rolls inside a narrow window of fat, sugar, and total solids. Too much water and it fractures into shards instead of curling; too much fat or sugar and it smears and will not set before it melts. This is why the single most successful operator in the category — Gil Grobe, 12M subscribers — makes his money selling a proprietary BASE POWDER "for the perfect Ice Cream Roll consistency" in his own webshop, and why Turkish suppliers sell "tava dondurma tozu" (pan ice cream powder) as a separate SKU. The recipe, not the pan, is the asset. For SHABIM this is where an Iraqi/Gulf flavour library — dates, cardamom, geymar-style richness, rose, tamarind, mango-amba adjacency — becomes a genuinely proprietary base book that no imported franchise has.

2. THE PHYSICS ENFORCES A SKILL GATE. The machine must be capable of −25 to −30 °C but is actually WORKED at a −18 to −21 °C surface. Below that the base freezes before it can be spread; above it, it never sets. The operator is managing a plate that is drifting in temperature all shift, in a Baghdad summer, while chopping mix-ins into it by hand. Two scrapers, 90 seconds, in front of the customer, with no second take. Trained staff are the constraint — and in a market with no existing rolled-ice-cream labour pool, whoever trains first owns the labour pool.

3. THE THROUGHPUT CEILING IS ALSO THE MOAT. Roughly 2–4 minutes of skilled hand-work per serving, per pan. That caps a single pan at roughly 15–25 servings per hour. ESTIMATE — derived from the 2–4 min/serving cycle time reported in equipment guides, not from an operator disclosure; treat as a planning figure, not a fact. This cuts both ways and the deck must model it honestly: it is why the queue outside 10Below and ROLL ICE CREAM FACTORY became the marketing (three-hour and five-hour lines respectively), and it is also why the format cannot absorb a demand spike. Multi-pan stations and a pre-portioned base system are the only levers. Whoever solves throughput without killing the performance wins the category.

4. IT CANNOT BE DELIVERED, WHOLESALED, OR PRE-MADE — WHICH IS BOTH SHIELD AND WOUND. The value is manufactured in front of the customer in 90 seconds and begins degrading immediately; the rolls slump from the outside in. No supermarket freezer version can compete, no cloud kitchen can knock you off, no industrial player can undercut you. But equally: in Baghdad and the Gulf, where delivery apps carry a large share of dessert volume, this format structurally forfeits that channel. Any SHABIM model that assumes delivery revenue on the rolls themselves is wrong. The rolls are the theatre that fills the store; a separate, delivery-stable product line has to carry the delivery P&L.

5. THE TRAP TO AVOID — the trend itself. Sweet Charlie's went 3 units (2017) → 17+ (2022) → 13 (today) at −5% growth. 10Below closed its St Marks Place, Allen Street and Los Angeles Little Tokyo locations. ROLL ICE CREAM FACTORY closed Fukuoka in August 2025 and suspended Ishigaki in October 2024. Every one of those was a single-product novelty business. The structural lesson is not "rolled ice cream fails" — it is that a shop selling ONLY the spectacle dies when the spectacle stops being new, typically 3–5 years after entry. The defensible version is rolled ice cream as one theatrical hero item inside a broader cold-drinks menu — which is exactly what SHABIM already is.
